  {
    "issue_type": "Path Traversal / Unvalidated File Access",
    "severity": "medium",
    "file": "t12.js",
    "line": 9,
    "evidence": "const file = path.join(NOTES_DIR, req.params.name);",
    "llm_reasoning": "While primarily a security concern, this has performance implications. An attacker can request files outside the intended directory, potentially hitting system files or large logs, causing the event loop to block on I/O for unexpected files. Furthermore, the lack of validation means the server will attempt to read any file path provided, leading to unnecessary disk I/O and potential resource exhaustion if many requests target large files.",
    "suggested_fix": "Validate that the resolved path starts with NOTES_DIR using path.resolve() and path.relative(). Example: const safePath = path.normalize(file); if (!safePath.startsWith(NOTES_DIR)) return res.status(403).send();",
    "confidence": 0.8,
    "agent_agreement": ["performance"]
  },
  {
    "issue_type": "Blocking I/O on large files",
    "severity": "medium",
    "file": "t12.js",
    "line": 10,
    "evidence": "fs.readFile(file, \"utf8\", (err, text) => { ... });",
    "llm_reasoning": "fs.readFile reads the entire file into memory before returning the response. If a user requests a very large file, this will consume significant heap memory, potentially triggering frequent Garbage Collection (GC) cycles or causing an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) error under concurrent load. Streaming the file using fs.createReadStream() is significantly more memory-efficient.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use streams to pipe the file content to the response: fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res);",
    "confidence": 0.9,
    "agent_agreement": ["performance"]
  }
]
